candidates.evidence: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसाम्... अनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् (consequence, loss, harm, and one's own capacity)

angle_en: Anupreksham: the refusal to weigh anything
angle_hi: अनपेक्ष्य: बिना सोचे-समझे शुरू किया गया कर्म

en.intro: Krishna has just described passionate action. Now he tells us about the worst kind. Listen for the four things a dark actor refuses to consider.
en.notice: Listen for the word anupreksham, without considering. A tamasic actor looks at the world and simply refuses to weigh the consequence, the loss, the harm, or their own capacity to finish it.
en.next: Krishna then describes the opposite kind of actor, one who is steady and unchanged by success or failure.
en.meaning: Action begun in delusion, ignoring its consequences, harm, and one’s own capacity, is called tamasic.

hi.meaning: जो कर्म परिणाम, हानि, हिंसा और सामर्थ्य को न देखकर मोहपूर्वक शुरू किया जाता है, वह तामस कहा जाता है।
hi.notice: अनपेक्ष्य शब्द सुनिए, जिसका अर्थ है बिना विचार किए। तामसिक कर्ता दुनिया को देखता है और बस परिणाम, हानि, हिंसा या अपनी क्षमता को तौलने से मना कर देता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण फिर उस कर्ता का वर्णन करते हैं जो सफलता या असफलता से नहीं बदलता, और जो स्थिर और उत्साही है।

issues: wrong_fact: "Listen for the word anupreksham, without considering." (The script quotes 'anupreksham', but the Sanskrit word in the verse is 'anpeksham' (अनपेक्ष्य). This is a factual error in the notice.)

unsupported: "कृष्ण ने अभी उत्साही कर्म का वर्णन किया है" (The previous verse (24) describes passionate action (rajasic), not enthusiastic action (sattvic). The Hindi intro misstates the nature of the previous verse as 'उत्साही' (enthusiastic), which actually belongs to the next verse (26, sattvic).)
